name: Asahi India Glass Ltd
_note: Fact base for the Asahi India Glass (AIS) initiation. Consolidated, Rs crore unless stated (results are filed in Rs lakh; divided by 100). Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026. FY = year to March (confirmed on Screener: Mar-2015 to Mar-2026 annual columns). Q1FY27 = Apr-Jun 2026. AIS holds no earnings calls or results presentations in our window: the results filings, the annual report and broker notes are the record. The Q2FY27 results (board meeting after our as-of date) and the Sep-2026 shareholding are not used.

profile.what: India's largest automotive-glass maker and one of three float-glass producers it owns: windshields (laminated), side and back lites (tempered), sunroofs, encapsulated and value-added glazing for passenger cars, commercial vehicles, railways and metros, plus white-goods glass; float glass, coated, reflective, mirror and processed architectural glass; and a consumer business (AIS Windows, Glasxperts, Windshield Experts with 151 service centres in 79 cities).
profile.jv: Began commercial operations in 1987 as a joint venture of the Labroo family, Asahi Glass Co. (now AGC Inc., Japan) and Maruti Udyog (now Maruti Suzuki India). Floatglass India (Taloja) merged into AIS in Sep-2003.
profile.plants: 15 manufacturing facilities and 11 sub-assembly units-cum-warehouses (AR FY26 p37); 14 plants listed in the BRSR incl. the Nashik unit commissioned in FY26. Float glass at Roorkee (Uttarakhand), Taloja (Maharashtra) and Soniyana (Rajasthan, third float line, commissioned in FY25 and used fully for in-house auto glass): 2,150 tonnes a day in total. Auto glass at Bawal, Chennai, Patan, Roorkee, Pune; an on-site assembly unit inside Maruti's Kharkhoda campus.
profile.capacity: Float 2,150 TPD; laminated ~10 mn+ pieces; tempered ~7.5 mn+ car sets (AR FY26 p37).

marketShare.pvGlassNote: ~80% of Indian passenger-vehicle glass (AR FY26 chairman's letter, BRSR); ~79% in the passenger-car segment (AR FY26 p38)

profile.customers: Every Indian car maker. Maruti Suzuki (a promoter, 10.59%) bought Rs872.97 cr in FY26 (17.5% of consolidated revenue; FY25 Rs656.93 cr) and Rs301.42 cr in Q1FY27 (21% of revenue). Shareholders approved related-party sales to Maruti of up to Rs1,500 cr in FY27 (AGM 18-Sep-2026). Exports 0.36% of standalone turnover.

shares.use: Prepayment and repayment of borrowings and general corporate purposes (fully used, AR FY26)
shares.src: AR FY26 notes 34 (EPS) and 12 (share capital); cash-flow statement (proceeds Rs994 cr net)

fy26.src: AR FY26 consolidated P&L, notes 25, 26, 34, 36, 46; chairman's letter (debt, ratios)

otherIncomeFY26.exceptional: FY26 Rs11.74 cr (labour-code past-service cost Rs7.20 cr and subsidiary merger costs Rs4.54 cr); FY25 +Rs31.83 cr (gain)

q1fy27.src: Q1FY27 results (consolidated P&L and segment table); Screener.in quarterly; AR FY26 AGM notice (Maruti RPT)

guidance.capex: Up to Rs2,000 cr approved (30-Jan-2026) for the next round of greenfield capacity in float, coatings and processing; no phasing given. Brownfield work continues at Patan (phase 3 started, phase 4 initiated), Chennai and Bawal (AR FY26 p110). FY26 capex Rs666 cr; FY25 Rs1,268 cr; FY24 Rs901 cr.
guidance.priorities: Chairman (AR FY26): 'We have completed a significant phase of investment. The next phase must be about consolidation, optimisation, superior cash generation and higher returns'; improve asset utilisation, working capital and ROCE (RoACE 11.6% in FY26).
guidance.float: Soniyana (third float line) stabilised and fully used for in-house raw glass for the automotive business (Jan-2026). Government imposed a minimum import price of Rs34,000/t on clear float glass for one year from 18-Aug-2026; anti-dumping duties on Malaysian clear float glass recommended for five more years after a 2026 sunset review (AR FY26 p28).
guidance.noCalls: AIS does not hold quarterly earnings calls; there is no numeric revenue or margin guidance.
guidance.src: Q3FY26 results letter; AR FY26; DGFT notification

history: Incorporated in 1984; commercial operations from 1987 as a joint venture of the Labroo family, Asahi Glass (Japan) and Maruti Udyog; first capital Rs1.87 cr
Floatglass India (Taloja float plant) merged into AIS: entry into float and architectural glass
Rights issue of Rs250 cr (second capital raise)
Float glass boom: segment EBIT Rs466 cr and Rs503 cr (31-34% EBITDA margin) on high import prices
Largest capex cycle in its history (Rs901 cr and Rs1,268 cr): third float line at Soniyana (Rajasthan), Roorkee float cold repair, Patan phase 2
QIP of Rs1,000 cr: 1.18 crore shares at Rs844.79; debt cut to Rs2,059 cr by Mar-2026
Four downstream subsidiaries merged into AIS Glass Solutions, renamed AIS Consumer Glass Solutions (Nov-2025)
Board approves up to Rs2,000 cr of greenfield capex in float, coatings and processing
Government sets a minimum import price on clear float glass for one year
historySrc: AR FY26 (chairman's letter, About AIS, board report, notes); AR FY22 (Floatglass India merger); results filings
management: Chairman & Managing Director (promoter, 11.47%); term from 19-Feb-2024 for five years
Whole-time Executive Director since Jan-2023 (33 years in automotive glass, earlier at AGC's automotive-glass OEM office); re-appointment for four years from Jan-2027 recommended
Non-executive director (promoter, relative of the CMD)
Non-executive director nominated by Maruti Suzuki, from Apr-2025
Non-executive director from Aug-2025 (replaced Masahiro Takeda on his retirement from AGC)
